"'''Because We Want To'''" is a song performed by English [[Pop music|pop]] singer [[Billie Piper|Billie]]. The song was written by Dion Rambo, Jacques Richmond, [[Skin Games|Wendy Page]], and Jim Marr and produced by Marr and Page for Billie's debut album, ''[[Honey to the B]]'' (1998). It was released as her debut [[single (music)|single]] on 29 June 1998 and entered the [[UK Singles Chart]] at number one in July 1998, making Billie the youngest artist to debut at number one, at age 15. It also reached the top 10 in Ireland, New Zealand, and Sweden. The song was the official theme of the [[1999 FIFA Women's World Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/drama/people/billie_piper_person_page.shtml|title=Drama – People Index Billie Piper|publisher=[[BBC]]|access-date=1 April 2014}}</ref>

"Because We Want To" is a song performed by English pop singer Billie. The song was written by Dion Rambo, Jacques Richmond, Wendy Page, and Jim Marr and produced by Marr and Page for Billie's debut album, Honey to the B (1998). It was released as her debut single on 29 June 1998 and entered the UK Singles Chart at number one in July 1998, making Billie the youngest artist to debut at number one, at age 15. It also reached the top 10 in Ireland, New Zealand, and Sweden. The song was the official theme of the 1999 FIFA Women's World Cup.

sections.heading: Chart performance
sections.wikitext: Selling over 80,000 copies during its opening week,<ref name="uksales">{{cite web|url=https://www.officialcharts.com/chart-news/official-chart-flashback-1998-billie-pipers-record-breaking-debut-at-number-1-with-because-we-want-to__19583/|title=Official Chart Flashback 1998: Billie Piper's record-breaking debut at Number 1 with Because We Want To|last=Copsey|first=Rob|publisher=[[Official Charts Company]]|date=6 July 2017|access-date=9 October 2020}}</ref> "Because We Want To" made [[Billie Piper|Billie]] the youngest artist to debut at number one on the [[UK Singles Chart]], aged 15. However, [[Helen Shapiro]] still holds the record as the youngest solo female singer to have topped the UK Singles Chart; "[[You Don't Know (Helen Shapiro song)|You Don't Know]]" rose to number one in 1961, when Shapiro was 14 years and 10 months old.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/uk/2008/jan/04/theatre.arts|title=Profile: Billie Piper {{!}} Television & radio|last=Pidd|first=Helen|newspaper=[[The Guardian]]|date=4 January 2008|access-date=9 January 2012|location=London}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.officialcharts.com/artist/9618/helen-shapiro/|title=Helen Shapiro|publisher=Official Charts Company|access-date=23 June 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine|title=Chart Commentary|last=Jones|first=Alan|magazine=Music Week|page=10|date=11 July 1998}}</ref> Outside the United Kingdom, the song became a top-10 hit in Ireland, New Zealand, and Sweden, peaking at numbers nine, nine, and eight, respectively.<ref name="charts"/> Although the song became a hit in Canada, peaking at number 14 on the [[Canadian Singles Chart]] and number 30 on the ''[[RPM (magazine)|RPM]]'' 100 Hit Tracks chart in September 1998, it did not chart in the United States.<ref name="csc"/><ref name="rpm"/><ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.billboard.com/music/billie|title=Billie Chart History|magazine=Billboard|access-date=23 June 2019}}</ref>
sections.text: Selling over 80,000 copies during its opening week, "Because We Want To" made Billie the youngest artist to debut at number one on the UK Singles Chart, aged 15. However, Helen Shapiro still holds the record as the youngest solo female singer to have topped the UK Singles Chart; "You Don't Know" rose to number one in 1961, when Shapiro was 14 years and 10 months old. Outside the United Kingdom, the song became a top-10 hit in Ireland, New Zealand, and Sweden, peaking at numbers nine, nine, and eight, respectively. Although the song became a hit in Canada, peaking at number 14 on the Canadian Singles Chart and number 30 on the RPM 100 Hit Tracks chart in September 1998, it did not chart in the United States.

sections.heading: Music video
sections.wikitext: The video (directed by Phil Griffin<ref>[http://www.mvdbase.com/video.php?id=3208 "Because We Want To" by Billie (mvdbase.com)]</ref>) starts in a run-down street in London, where the ground is violently shaking. The reason is soon seen: A [[Unidentified flying object|UFO]] is flying just metres from the ground. Billie is then seen teleporting from the ship and down onto the street. She starts singing and dancing and soon gathers huge crowds of supporters. In the video, cut scenes of Billie and her friends walking down side streets are seen. In one scene, she melts a bin which transforms into a dancing humanoid and in another scene she [[graffiti]]s "Billie" on a billboard and an animated character then jumps from the billboard and dances along with the humanoid made from the melted bin. Later in the video, she and her friends sneak into a warehouse and have a party.
